page: The UpCloud GPU-20xCPU-256GB-3xL40S is a GPU-accelerated server configured with an AMD EPYC 9575F processor built on the x86_64 architecture. This system provides 20 vCPUs across 20 physical cores with a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. It features 256.0 GB of system memory, yielding 12.8 GB of RAM per core. Acceleration is driven by three NVIDIA L40S GPUs from the Ada Lovelace architecture, delivering a combined 144 GB of VRAM. The server operates on a KVM hypervisor and does not include local storage.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core scoring 4190.38 and single-threaded gzip compression reaching 38.86 GB/sec. Multi-core performance is strong, as evidenced by a stress-ng multi-core score of 84070.24 and a PassMark CPU score of 62711.03. Memory bandwidth is highly capable, registering 3984.93 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 306.94 GB/sec for large-block reads. Database operations are supported by a PassMark database score of 27020.33 and Redis SET performance of 81.97 million operations per second.

From a resource density perspective, this server offers high qualitative cost efficiency for parallel processing and graphics-heavy workloads due to the inclusion of three enterprise-grade GPUs and a large memory footprint. However, the lack of local storage requires external storage solutions, which may introduce latency tradeoffs. The shared CPU allocation model is another consideration for sustained, non-GPU compute tasks. This configuration is highly suited for GPU-accelerated workloads, machine learning model training, AI inference, large-scale data science jobs, and parallelized scientific simulations.

Operating on a KVM hypervisor, this server lacks local storage, requiring external storage configurations. Benchmarks show top-tier single-core performance, with stress-ng scoring 4190.38, and strong multi-core capabilities, including a PassMark CPU score of 62711.03. Memory bandwidth is robust, reaching 306.94 GB/sec for large-block reads.
